title: Build the GitHub spec pipeline and commit the generated client (step 3.3)
body:
Step 3.3 of the split plan: the GitHub spec pipeline. It pins GitHub's REST description, keeps the spec fixes as a reviewed list applied by a Swift transform (decision 4), and commits the generated client. The spike's code (swift-steward#21) was ported onto `main`; that branch isn't merged or continued.

## What's here

- **`Specs/github/`**
  - `upstream.env` is the pin: commit `bb75494` of `github/rest-api-description` (2026-10-17) and the file's SHA-256. Upstream has cut no release since 2022, so there's no tag to pin to.
  - `fixes.yaml` is the fix list, one entry per fix. Each has a `name`, a `why`, the recorded `fixture` for corrections of upstream, and one `edit`.
  - `openapi-generator-config.yaml` keeps the five operations v1 needs.
  - `openapi.yaml` is the generator's input, filtered and fixed. It's written by the pipeline and committed for review.
- **`Tooling/`** is a nested package, so the root manifest never pulls in the generator.
  - The `GitHubSpecFixes` engine supports six kinds of edit. Each checks its precondition. A fix that upstream has made redundant fails with "drop the fix", and one whose target moved fails with "update the fix", both naming the fix. One run reports every stale fix, not just the first.
  - The list checks itself: names are unique, every entry has a `why`, and every correction names a fixture.
  - `github-spec-fix` is the command (ArgumentParser).
  - `generate-github-api.sh` is the one command: download, verify the SHA-256 (of the cached copy too), filter, fix, generate. It writes the committed outputs only after every step succeeds.
  - `check-github-api-drift.sh` is the drift guard.
- **`Sources/GitHubAPI/Generated/`** holds the generated client: 5,412 lines (the spike's had 12,207). The root manifest adds only `swift-openapi-runtime` and `swift-openapi-urlsession`, and only the `GitHubAPI` target uses them (decision 5).
- **`.github/workflows/github-api.yml`** runs the drift guard on PRs that touch the spec, the client, its tests, or `Tooling/`. It runs the Tooling tests, regenerates, and fails on any difference, untracked files included.
- **`docs/github-api.md`** covers the pipeline, updating the pin, and adding a fix. AGENTS.md now states the dependency rule and the commands. `.gitattributes` marks the generated files `linguist-generated`, so PR diffs collapse them.

The current fixes:

| Fix | Kind | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `update-comment-404` | correction: `addResponse` | `issues-update-comment.macos-update-deleted.http` |
| `delete-comment-404` | correction: `addResponse` | `issues-delete-comment.macos-delete-deleted.http` |
| `drop-x-webhooks` | adapts the description: `remove` | none needed: `filter` keeps 20,000 lines of root vendor extension that the generator never reads |
| `repository-has-downloads-undeprecated`, `repository-squash-title-undeprecated` | adapts the description: `undeprecate` | the warning-free build: the generated initializers would warn |

## Decisions

- **The fix list is YAML (`Specs/github/fixes.yaml`), not Swift values.** The pin and the fixes change together when the pin moves, and this keeps them in one folder, as the done criteria and the plan's layout have it. Adding or dropping a fix doesn't touch Swift code. The `why` fields and comments read as the review record. Swift values would add compile-time checking, but the decoder and `SpecFixList`'s rules give the same at the start of every run: an unknown kind of edit, a missing field, a duplicate name, or a correction without a fixture all fail.
- **The drift guard runs on Linux (`swift:6.2`).** The spike had left open whether Linux regenerates the same bytes. It does, with one fix: a cold rerun on macOS found the pipeline wasn't deterministic. `filter` writes the keys of `x-github` extensions and examples in hash order, and Swift seeds its hashing per process, so each run reordered about 450 lines of `openapi.yaml`. The generated Swift didn't change. The script now sets `SWIFT_DETERMINISTIC_HASHING=1`. With it, repeated runs agree, and a cold run in `swift:6.2` (Swift 6.2) matches macOS 26 (Swift 6.4) byte for byte. Linux is also the cheaper runner.
- **The webhook payload schemas are no longer in the filter.** The spike recommended this for 4.2: read the event's `pull_request` with the REST `PullRequest` schema. It shrinks the output from 12,207 to 5,412 lines and makes one of the spike's three deprecation fixes unnecessary.
- **The generated code keeps the strict settings.** `accessModifier: internal` and the two `undeprecate` fixes keep it warning-free on macOS, and on Linux under `-warnings-as-errors`, so it needs no relaxed target. SwiftLint excludes `Generated/`, and now covers `Tooling/`.
- **Coverage.** The ruleset's `code_coverage` rule (minimum 70%, at most a 1-point drop) reads line coverage only from Cobertura reports that a workflow uploads with `actions/upload-code-coverage`, which needs GitHub Code Quality. No workflow uploads one, and Code Quality is off, so the rule passes with no data: the rule suite for this repo's last push shows `code_coverage: pass`. There's nothing to exclude `Generated/` from yet, so this PR doesn't add an upload. `docs/github-api.md` records that the exclusion is needed and how to make it (`llvm-cov export -ignore-filename-regex='Sources/GitHubAPI/Generated/'`), with these measurements (in-process line coverage, so the CLI, which the tests run as a subprocess, isn't counted):

  | | Lines | Covered |
  |---|---|---|
  | Hand-written sources | 388 | 97.7% |
  | `Generated/` | 2,435 | 55.9% |
  | Both | 2,823 | 61.6%, under the 70% minimum |

- **Brought from 3.4, because it was cheap:** the spike's recorded fixtures and the offline decoding suite (`FixtureDecodingTests`), on a read-only `RecordedResponse` and `FixtureTransport`. Not brought: the live test, the recording middleware, and the event-payload tests, which need the webhook schemas or the 4.2 decision.

## Tests run

All on macOS 26 (Xcode with Swift 6.4) unless marked Linux, on this branch.

| Command | Inputs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `swift test` (network tests on) | full suite | 48 tests in 12 suites, plus 9 in `GitHubAPITests`: pass |
| `xcodebuild test -scheme swift-steward-Package -destination platform=macOS` | full suite | TEST SUCCEEDED (48 + 9), no compiler warnings |
| `swift build --build-tests` (cold) | whole package | no warnings |
| `swift test --package-path Tooling` | 20 tests: every kind of edit, refusals, missing targets, YAML decoding, list rules, string-typed enum values, the repository's own list | pass |
| `swiftlint lint --quiet`, `actionlint`, `shellcheck -x Tooling/*.sh` | whole tree | silent / clean |
| `Tooling/check-github-api-drift.sh` | after the last commit | matches |
| Linux, `swift:6.2` container | `swift test --package-path Tooling`; `swift build --build-tests -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors`; `swift test --skip-build --filter GitHubAPITests` | 18 tests (before the singular-message test), build clean, 9 tests: pass |

End-to-end checks:

| Check | How | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A cold regeneration reproduces the commit | `rm -rf Tooling/.build && Tooling/check-github-api-drift.sh` (no tools, no spec cache) | "matches the pipeline's output", exit 0, tree clean |
| Linux regenerates the same bytes | the full pipeline in `swift:6.2` from a cold spec cache, then `cmp`/`diff -r` against the macOS output | identical |
| The drift guard fails on a hand edit | committed a throwaway edit to `Generated/Client.swift` plus an added file, then ran the guard | exit 1, `::error::`, both files listed |
| …and on a generated file missing from the commit | throwaway commit deleting `Types+Components+Headers.swift` | exit 1, `?? …Headers.swift` |
| A checksum mismatch stops the pipeline | (a) appended a byte to the cached spec; (b) set a wrong `SPEC_SHA256`, which forces a download | both exit 1 with expected and actual SHA-256; the bad copy is deleted; nothing in the tree changes |
| A fix that upstream has made redundant fails and names the fix | (a) applied `update-comment-404` to the filtered spec, as if upstream had, then ran the real list on it; (b) added a `pulls-get-404` entry that upstream already satisfies and ran the one command | (a) exit 1: "update-comment-404: upstream already declares 404 for patch …; drop the fix", and no other fix named; (b) exit 1 naming `pulls-get-404`, outputs untouched |
| The client decodes each fix's fixture, and fails without the fix | `SpecFixRegressionTests`; then dropped both 404 fixes, regenerated, and ran it again | pass with the fixes; without them the tests don't compile (`Output has no member 'notFound'`) |
| Every fix reports its own result as redundant | `RepositoryFixListTests` applies the list to the committed `openapi.yaml` | all five fail as redundant, by name, in order |
| `steward` is unchanged | 27 commands with the v2.0.0 release binary (`/opt/homebrew/bin/steward`) and this branch's release build: `--version`, the help texts, `changes` on swift-pr-70000, swift-argument-parser, redis, the kernel 6.6→6.7 diff and this branch's diff (json and text), and `filter` with every tool, format, `--tolerance`/`--repo-root`, stdin, and `--fail-on` | stdout, stderr and exit codes `cmp`-identical for all 27 |

## Review

`codex review --base main` (codex-cli 0.164.0, `gpt-6.1-sol`) reported one finding, printed twice:

| Finding | What I did |
|---|---|
| [P2] `addEnumValue` builds the new value as an implicitly typed Yams scalar, so `"true"`, `"1"` or `"null"` serialize as a bool, a number or null, and the generator rejects them for a string enum | **Fixed** in 31892e7: the value is now a single-quoted `!!str` scalar. The regression test round-trips five values through serialization, and four of them (`true`, `1`, `null`, a date) failed before the fix. No current fix adds an enum value, so the generated output doesn't change. |

Codex couldn't run the Swift toolchain in its sandbox, so it reviewed without running the tests.
